s1.syndrome_frame: subacute onset of respiratory symptoms in a patient with a history of rheumatologic disease and recent initiation of immunosuppressive therapy
salient_findings: ground-glass interstitial infiltrates on chest CT
key_facts: 41-year-old woman
3-month history of sacroiliac pain, arthralgias, and lower-limb myalgias
recent initiation of etanercept
development of respiratory symptoms after the third dose of etanercept
absence of fever, hemoptysis, chest pain, or other systemic symptoms
normal oxygenation on room air
scant basal crackles on pulmonary auscultation
normal laboratory studies except for mild eosinophilia
ground-glass interstitial infiltrates on chest CT
centrifugal distribution of infiltrates predominantly in the upper lobes
mosaic pattern of disseminated attenuation on chest CT
normal echocardiogram and ECG

shortlist.label: Etanercept-induced interstitial lung disease
shortlist.why_kept: Recent initiation of etanercept and development of respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Mild eosinophilia and ground-glass interstitial infiltrates on chest CT

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of rheumatologic disease and interstitial lung disease

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Ground-glass interstitial infiltrates and mosaic pattern of disseminated attenuation on chest CT

shortlist.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of respiratory symptoms and absence of fever or other systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient developed respiratory symptoms after the third dose of etanercept, with ground-glass interstitial infiltrates on chest CT and scant basal crackles, which is consistent with etanercept-induced interstitial lung disease, a known adverse effect of TNF-alpha inhibitors like etanercept.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic pneumonia
rejected.why: Mild eosinophilia is present, but the clinical and radiological findings are more consistent with an interstitial lung disease related to etanercept use rather than eosinophilic pneumonia.

rejected.label: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease
rejected.why: The patient has seronegative spondyloarthropathy, not rheumatoid arthritis, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of lymphadenopathy, granulomas, or other systemic symptoms typical of sarcoidosis.

rejected.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: The temporal relationship between etanercept initiation and respiratory symptoms, along with the radiological findings, points more towards an etanercept-induced condition rather than cryptogenic organizing pneumonia.
